Rep. Brad Sherman (D-CA) introduced the 'Stop Oil Exports to Lower Gas Prices Act' to temporarily ban U.S. crude oil, gasoline, and diesel exports during the conflict with Iran. The bill aims to lower gasoline prices and protect U.S. consumers from global energy-market disruptions by amending Section 101 of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2016. It would prohibit exports until the president certifies that military operations against Iran have ceased and the Strait of Hormuz is fully reopened. The president could waive the ban for oil that cannot be efficiently refined in the U.S. Sherman argues that restricting exports would increase domestic supply and ease price pressures.
